title: JSON Mode Coverage Metering + Probability Calibration Harness
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Purpose: Build a test harness and instrumentation to measure how well ‘JSON mode’ adheres to schema constraints under realistic sampling conditions and streaming/toolcall interleaving, and to quantify probability mass allocation to valid schema tokens (probability calibration). This will inform gating thresholds, fallback policies, and whether to recommend constrained decoding or soft enforcement for different product tiers.

Scope: generate deterministic and stochastic samples across multiple models and temperatures; measure token-level and object-level coverage; run adversarial prompts and partial-stream scenarios (toolcall interleaves, truncated sequences). Include a lightweight runtime shim that can compute a streaming coverage score and expose it to the router/console for experiments. Exclude production rollout of gating policy (this ticket covers test harness + dashboards + initial recommendations).

Motivation: We have lots of isolated contract tests that assert binary pass/fail for JSON mode. Real-world traffic is noisy (temperature, top_p, decoding errors, tooling interleaves). We need a quantitative calibration signal (how much probability mass does the model place on syntactically valid schema tokens) to: 1) tune constrained decoding fallbacks, 2) set alerting thresholds for regressions, 3) decide when to prefer soft repair strategies vs strict-mode aborts.

Non-goals: building production rejection UI, changes to API surface, or infra-backed gating enforcement in Dedicated/Private (tracked separately).
test_matrix: Baseline: greedy and sampling (temp 0.0, 0.3, 0.7) across 3 model sizes; 1k seed prompts covering single-object, nested-object, arrays-of-objects
Streaming partial-object: simulate token-truncated streams and compute running coverage every 50 tokens
Interleaved toolcalls: inject toolcall tokens (function_start/function_end) at random offsets and verify coverage/repair behavior
Adversarial prompts: five classes that provoke schema drift (ambiguous instructions, extra prose, disallowed keys, similar-but-invalid types)
Constraint-lift experiments: compare constrained-decoder (bias/force tokens) vs logit-adjustment soft penalties at matched latency budgets
Cross-model calibration: run same seed set on three model families to measure variance
Beam vs nucleus: evaluate beam search and top_p variants for object-level correctness and token-prob distributions
Throughput/latency sweep: measure harness overhead at 64/256/1024 concurrent streams
instrumentation: Token-level coverage: fraction of generated tokens that match schema-expected tokens (streaming and final)
Object-level correctness: JSON parses and schema validation pass/fail
Probability mass on valid token set: cumulative log-prob assigned to tokens that keep structure valid
Calibration metrics: Brier score and ECE-style bins on per-token validity probability
False-repair rate: cases where soft-repair produced syntactic but semantically wrong outputs
Latency overhead: average p95 added by coverage-meter per request
Dashboard: /dashboards/jsonmode-coverage with breakdown by model, temp, prompt-type
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: design doc reviewed with Applied ML (Priya) and Runtime (Marco). Agreed on probe-based instrumentation instead of full constrained-decoder-instrumentation to reduce initial infra changes.
2026-03-11 - Prototype: implemented a micro-harness that replays sampling traces and computes token validity masks. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-harness/pull/214
2026-03-12 - Review feedback: Runtime asked to limit per-request CPU and avoid blocking token loop during streaming; updated shim to run async with sampling window of 128 tokens.
2026-03-13 - Data run started: 10k prompts across 3 models queued on qa-cluster. Initial dashboard stub at https://internal.redwood/dash/json-coverage/ENG-472819
risks_mitigations: Risk: Per-request instrumentation may add measurable latency under high qps. Mitigation: sampling-based probe (run coverage every Nth request) and async aggregation

Risk: Calibration varies dramatically across models and temps, making hard thresholds brittle. Mitigation: compute model+temp-specific baselines and surface relative regressions instead of absolute thresholds
Risk: Toolcall tokens may be treated differently across runtimes. Mitigation: canonicalize toolcall tokenization in harness before computing coverage masks
Risk: False confidence when schema accepts many tokens (open enums). Mitigation: compute effective schema entropy and normalize coverage by schema branching factor
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run end-to-end synthetic suite and produce coverage + calibration metrics for at least 3 models and 3 temperature settings
Dashboard shows token-level coverage, model-temp baselines, and an alert rule example for a 15% relative drop in coverage
PRs merged for the harness (ci-harness/pull/214) and for async coverage shim in runtime (runtime/runs/PR-789)
Recommendations doc committed: when to prefer constrained decoding vs soft penalty for streaming JSON mode
Latency overhead measured and documented with mitigation plan if p95 increases > 30ms
